title: Quilt Platform 26.11.0 Upgrade Guide
summary: The complete checklist for upgrading a Quilt Platform stack to 26.11.0: IAM and service control policy changes, Lake Formation requirements, secret rotation, and post-upgrade steps.
body_markdown:
Quilt Platform 26.11.0


The complete upgrade checklist for stack administrators, from 26.9.x to 26.11.0. Work through **Before updating** first: several items change what IAM, Lake Formation, and service control policies must allow, and skipping them can fail the update or lock users out of data.


Each item below names the stacks it applies to. Items tagged **Security** close an exposure; apply them even if the rest of the release can wait. Questions at any step:support@quilt.bio .


## Before updating


Policy, template, and account changes to make before you apply the 26.11.0 template.


Security


Stacks with unmanaged roles


An unmanaged role in the stack's account whose trust policy's principal is the account (` arn:aws:iam::<account>:root` ) rather than the registry's role, even with a condition naming the registry's role, can no longer be assumed after this update, so its users get no credentials: name the stack's` RegistryRoleARN` output in its trust policy, as[Preparing an AWS Role for use with Quilt](https://docs.quilt.bio/quilt-platform-administrator/technical-reference#preparing-an-aws-role-for-use-with-quilt) shows. An unmanaged role in another account registered under one of the account-administration role names that page lists, or with a wildcard or a policy variable in its ARN, is no longer handed out; an edit to a role so named or with such an ARN must give it an allowed role's ARN


Security


Stacks whose users open buckets outside the stack, or public buckets without a grant


Add to the stack any bucket outside it that users open in the catalog, such as one holding package entries, metadata schemas or saved queries, and grant a role any public bucket in the stack its users read without a grant: the catalog no longer reads either, and for an anonymous viewer reads only what every default role is granted. To show a custom` s3://` logo on the sign-in page of a stack that requires sign-in, keep it in the service bucket, where the theme editor uploads logos


Security


Stacks whose` package_handle` templates use more than` username` and` directory`


A bucket's` package_handle` template that uses anything but` username` and` directory` must be rewritten with only those two, or the package dialog pre-fills the username prefix in its place


Security


On the stack-wide package tables, a principal that can set` quilt:stack` (see Credentials and roles), tag` ManagedUserRole` or edit its trust policy reads a role's rows, so an account policy must deny` iam:CreateRole` ,` iam:TagRole` ,` iam:CreateUser` ,` iam:TagUser` and` sts:TagSession` where` ForAnyValue:StringEqualsIgnoreCase` matches` quilt:stack` in` aws:TagKeys` , and, on each stack's` ManagedUserRole` ,` iam:TagRole` whatever the key and` iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy` , to every principal but the one CloudFormation deploys each Quilt stack as, its service role where it has one, as the example policy in[Reserving the quilt:stack tag key](https://docs.quilt.bio/quilt-platform/advanced/iceberg-tables#reserving-the-quilt-stack-tag-key) does, and that section also lists the other paths to the key and the policies that close them; no role's trust policy may let SAML or OIDC federation pass` quilt:stack` as a session tag. Lake Formation's row filters bind Athena, not S3: a principal with S3 read on the service bucket's` package-tables/` prefix reads every bucket's rows


A service control policy or other account policy must allow the registry role` sts:TagSession` with the` quilt:role:*` and` quilt:user` keys, or every vend of a managed role's credentials fails. A role assumed from a managed role's vended credentials must now allow` sts:TagSession` in its trust policy and in every policy that allows` sts:AssumeRole` on it,` ManagedUserRoleExtraPolicies` and the managed role's Quilt policies alike, or` AssumeRole` is refused with "not authorized to perform: sts:TagSession". The stack's tags, which CloudFormation copies onto` ManagedUserRole` , share the role's 50-tag limit with` quilt:stack` and the Partner Revenue Measurement tag, so a stack already carrying 49 tags fails this update; a downgrade, or a failed update's rollback, fails managed roles' credential vends for the minutes it takes to replace the registry's tasks


The update that adds the Partner Revenue Measurement tag fails if a stack resource already carries its type's tag limit, counting tags copied from the stack: 50 for most types, the search domain and IAM roles included. It also fails where a tag policy or SCP denies the key` aws-apn-id-730278974607`


Stacks deployed through a scoped CloudFormation service role


A CloudFormation service role scoped like the installation guide's example needs` iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy` and` iam:UntagRole` , now in the example, to apply or roll back this release. It also needs` lambda:PutFunctionEventInvokeConfig` ,` lambda:GetFunctionEventInvokeConfig` ,` lambda:UpdateFunctionEventInvokeConfig` and` lambda:DeleteFunctionEventInvokeConfig` for every stack's invoke configurations, the stack-wide package tables' among them, and` lambda:GetFunctionRecursionConfig` ,` glue:GetDatabase` ,` logs:DescribeIndexPolicies` ,` logs:GetDataProtectionPolicy` ,` lakeformation:DescribeLakeFormationIdentityCenterConfiguration` ,` lakeformation:DescribeResource` and` lakeformation:ListResources` for creating the tables' database, functions and log groups; the example now carries them all. The example role grants every action that adds the Partner Revenue Measurement tag but lacks these actions that remove it, which a failed update's rollback, or a downgrade, uses on resources already tagged:` athena:UntagResource` ,` cloudtrail:RemoveTags` ,` ec2:DeleteTags` ,` ecs:UntagResource` ,` elasticloadbalancing:RemoveTags` ,` es:RemoveTags` ,` events:UntagResource` ,` firehose:UntagDeliveryStream` ,` kms:UntagResource` ,` lambda:UntagResource` ,` logs:UntagResource` ,` rds:RemoveTagsFromResource` ,` secretsmanager:UntagResource` ,` servicediscovery:UntagResource` ,` sns:UntagResource` ,` sqs:UntagQueue` ,` ssm:RemoveTagsFromResource` ,` synthetics:UntagResource` ,` wafv2:UntagResource` . Without them a rollback can stop in` UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED` ; add them to the role and continue the rollback. CloudFormation may also call` ecs:ListTagsForResource` ,` servicediscovery:ListTagsForResource` ,` athena:ListTagsForResource` ,` sns:ListTagsForResource` and` es:ListTags` when it updates these resources' tags, and the example lacks them; grant them before updating


Stacks whose service bucket is backed up, replicated or copied in bulk


The service bucket reserves` qurator-skills/` for the registry, which keeps Qurator skills there: its bucket policy denies object access under that prefix to every other principal, so a backup, replication or bulk copy of the service bucket now stops at it


The registry now calls Lake Formation at every deploy and at every admin's edit of a role's buckets, so Lake Formation must be reachable from the registry's VPC, as Glue, Athena, IAM and STS are, and allowed by the account's service control policies. Where it is not, admins' edits of policies and managed roles fail, and no user can read the stack-wide package tables until the registry's migration, run at each release's update, first reaches Lake Formation; after that, the registry's failure to call it takes no reads from users, but no role reads the rows of a bucket first added to the stack while that failure lasts, until the migration next reaches it


Updating to this release creates the stack-wide package tables, and the registry's migration task fills them from every registered bucket without holding up the update; the next release's update completes a fill that stopped short. On an account that enforces Lake Formation the tables need` EnableLakeFormationGrants` set to` Enabled` , and a managed role already reading more than 100 buckets reads nothing of them until its buckets are split across roles


Stacks with packages whose name begins with an underscore in either part


Updating a stack to this release, or adding a bucket to a stack that runs it, fills the stack-wide package tables without the revisions and tags of packages whose name begins with an underscore in either part, such as` _team/data` or` team/_data` , though with their manifests and entries, and a later deploy does not add them; the tables record a later revision of such a package, with the` latest` tag it moves. The documentation's "Querying packages with Iceberg tables" page says which of them the per-bucket tables hold


The stack-wide package tables' two functions reserve 3 concurrent executions between them, so an update to this release fails on an account that cannot reserve them above Lambda's unreserved-concurrency minimum. The functions that forward S3's native EventBridge events and package-revision events, also new on every stack, reserve 10 and 5 more, 18 in all


Updating to this release creates a Glue database named` quilt__` and the stack's name in lower case, every character outside` a-z` and` 0-9` replaced by` _` . The update fails at its creation and rolls back where a database of that name exists, as it does for the second of two stacks in one account and region whose names differ only in case


Stacks with Voila


Updating to this release deletes the stack's Voila resources, among them its EC2 instance, ECS service and load balancer rule. A stack that passes` VoilaVersion` or` VoilaAMI` explicitly, in a CLI parameter list or in Terraform, must stop passing them in the same update that moves it to this release: CloudFormation rejects an update that passes a parameter the template no longer has


Stacks that query the per-bucket Iceberg tables


The per-bucket Iceberg tables are deprecated: they keep working in this release, and a later release removes them in favor of the stack-wide package tables, which carry the bucket as their` registry` column


A rollback of the update to this release, a downgrade past it or the stack's deletion removes the stack-wide package tables but leaves their` package-tables/` prefix registered with Lake Formation and its files in the service bucket. The documentation's "Querying packages with Iceberg tables" page gives the steps that clear them, before a downgrade or deletion and before an update that failed is retried


## After updating


Rotations, cleanups, and reviews once the stack is on 26.11.0.


Security


The upgrade signs every user out and revokes Connect access tokens at once, but leaves API keys and passwords as they are, and AWS credentials issued before it stay valid for up to an hour: from an hour after the upgrade, review API keys with` quilt3.admin.api_keys` , users and admins, and the SSO configuration's mappings, and remove any you do not recognize, since a key or an account made with a stolen session outlives the sign-out; have users who may have been exposed change their passwords


Security


Admins are advised to press "Revoke all API keys" in Admin → Settings → Security once after upgrading to this release, after telling key owners to expect to issue a new one


Security


Users' session tokens the S3 proxy already logged stay valid until their sessions end, and the log streams the S3 proxy wrote before the upgrade still hold them: delete those, prefixed` s3-proxy/` in the log group named after the stack


Security


Stacks given an` AdminPassword`


Task-definition revisions from before this release keep the` AdminPassword` value they were given, readable to any principal allowed` ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition` : CloudFormation deregisters a superseded revision but does not delete it. If the admin still signs in with that password, reset it from the catalog's sign-in page, since changing` AdminPassword` does nothing to an existing admin; until then, deleting the inactive revisions (` aws ecs delete-task-definitions` ) stops it being read there. On a stack with sign-in through an SSO provider, those revisions hold an empty` AdminPassword` , so there is nothing to clean


Security


Task-definition revisions from before this release keep the database password and the SSO client secrets in plain text, and` DescribeTaskDefinition` still returns them: each stack update leaves the previous revision INACTIVE instead of deleting it. Rotate the database password (the one in` DBUrl` , or` DBPassword` ) and the SSO client secrets; an admin who cannot rotate yet can delete the INACTIVE revisions (` aws ecs delete-task-definitions` ), which removes readable copies of a still-valid value but undoes no read already made


Security


Stacks deployed with Terraform from quiltdata/iac


On a stack deployed with Terraform from[quiltdata/iac](https://github.com/quiltdata/iac) , Terraform generates the database password and builds` DBUrl` from it, so once the stack runs this release, rotate the password with` terraform apply -replace='<address>'` , where` <address>` is the stack's own line of` terraform state list | grep module.db.module.db.random_password` , and redeploy the services as below right after it: their new database connections fail until then, so plan a maintenance window. A reset in the RDS console, which Terraform does not detect, or a stack update that fails during the apply leaves` DBUrl` and the stack's secret on the old password, so the services' new connections fail until the same` -replace` and redeploy run


Stacks whose database needs migrations


A new password for the same database needs no migrations, but a database that needs them, such as an empty one, one restored from a snapshot taken before this release, or the new one a` DBUser` change creates on a stack with its own database, needs the migration task run once before the services are redeployed. Run it with` aws ecs run-task --cluster <stack> --task-definition <stack>-registry-migration --launch-type FARGATE --network-configuration <config>` , where` <config>` is the` networkConfiguration` that` aws ecs describe-services --cluster <stack> --services <stack>-bulk-scanner` returns


Once a stack runs this release, an update that changes only` DBUrl` ,` DBPassword` or an SSO client secret changes that value's Secrets Manager secret but no task definition, so it neither restarts running tasks nor reruns the database migrations: redeploy` <stack>-registry` and, for the database,` <stack>-bulk-scanner` and, where Qurator is enabled,` <stack>-batch-summarizer` , with` aws ecs update-service --cluster <stack> --service <service> --force-new-deployment` . A service whose own task definition changes in the same update, as these do in an upgrade that ships a new registry image, needs no extra step


Stacks whose policies restrict third-party scripts


For the Help panel's chat with Quilt support and sales, the catalog loads HubSpot's script from` js.hs-scripts.com` on every page. Some customer variants are exempt, and an admin can turn the chat widget off from Admin → Settings


Stacks with the Benchling integration


Changing` pkg_prefix` does not move existing entry packages; each entry's package is created under the new name the next time it is packaged. If the bucket's Quilt workflow sets a` handle_pattern` , it must accept the new namespaces


For the full picture of what 26.11.0 ships, see the release email, or writesupport@quilt.bio for the complete notes. Upgrade mechanics live in the[upgrade documentation](https://docs.quilt.bio/quilt-platform-administration/installation#routine-maintenance-and-upgrades) .
